title: Arithmetic and Geometric Progressions
seo_title: Sequences and Series – SSS 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the nth term and the sum of arithmetic and geometric progressions; find means; sum to infinity; solve word problems. (summary of the NERDC SSS 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 maths worksheets on sequences and series: AP and GP, nth term, sum of n terms, arithmetic and geometric means, sum to infinity and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • In an AP you add the same number d each time; in a GP you multiply by the same ratio r.
  • AP: Sₙ = n/2 (2a + (n − 1)d). GP: Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1).
  • When −1 < r < 1, the sum to infinity of a GP is a ÷ (1 − r).

Examples

Example

3, 7, 11, … Find T₂₀

a = 3, d = 4

3 + 19 × 4

Answer: 79

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using n instead of n − 1T₁ = a, so use (n − 1)d.
Finding d the wrong way roundd = second term − first term.
Sum to infinity when |r| ≥ 1It only exists when −1 < r < 1.

items.q: What is the next term? 11, 8, 5, 2, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: subtract 3 each time. 2 − 3 = −1.

items.q: What is the next term? 5, −2, −9, −16, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: subtract 7 each time. −16 − 7 = −23.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, …
items.e: The difference is always 4, so it is arithmetic.

items.q: What is the next term? 4, 8, 16, 32, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 2 each time. 32 × 2 = 64.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, …
items.e: Each term is the one before × 2, so it is geometric.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, …
items.e: The differences change (7, 9, 11, 13) and there is no common ratio, so it is neither.

items.q: What is the next term? 5, 20, 80, 320, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 4 each time. 320 × 4 = 1,280.

items.q: What is the next term? 3, 15, 75, 375, …
items.e: This is geometric: multiply by 5 each time. 375 × 5 = 1,875.

items.q: What is the next term? 5, 2, −1, −4, …
items.e: This is arithmetic: subtract 3 each time. −4 − 3 = −7.

items.q: Is this sequence arithmetic, geometric or neither? 13, 18, 23, 28, 33, …
items.e: The difference is always 5, so it is arithmetic.

items.q: Which of these lists is not an arithmetic progression?
items.e: 2, −3, 4, −5, …: the differences are not equal, so it is not an AP.

items.q: Write the next term of the AP −9, 3, 15, 27, …
items.e: Add d = 12 to the last term: 27 + (12) = 39.

items.e: In an AP the difference between consecutive terms is always the same. Only −15, −9, −3, 3, … has a constant difference (6).

items.q: Write the next term of the AP −14, −20, −26, −32, …
items.e: Add d = −6 to the last term: −32 + (−6) = −38.

items.q: Find the common difference of the AP −8, −152, −7, −132, …

For what value of k are 1k + 3, 3k + 3 and 6k consecutive terms of an AP?
items.e: Middle term × 2 = sum of the outer terms: 2(3k + 3) = (1k + 3) + (6k), so k = 3.

items.q: Find the 5th term from the last term of the AP 10, 16, 22, …, 250.
items.e: Count back from the last term: 250 − (5 − 1)(6) = 226.

For what value of k are 3k − 1, 2k + 5 and 5k − 1 consecutive terms of an AP?
items.e: Middle term × 2 = sum of the outer terms: 2(2k + 5) = (3k − 1) + (5k − 1), so k = 3.

items.q: For what value of k are 2k + 1, 3k + 3 and 6k − 7 consecutive terms of an AP?
items.e: Middle term × 2 = sum of the outer terms: 2(3k + 3) = (2k + 1) + (6k − 7), so k = 6.

items.q: For what value of k are 3k − 1, 4k + 1 and 7k − 11 consecutive terms of an AP?
items.e: Middle term × 2 = sum of the outer terms: 2(4k + 1) = (3k − 1) + (7k − 11), so k = 7.

items.q: The 9th term of an AP is −10 and its 28th term is −29. Find its 48th term.
Find the 10th term from the last term of the AP 13, 14, 15, …, 56.
items.e: Count back from the last term: 56 − (10 − 1)(1) = 47.

items.e: Divide a term by the one before: 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

items.q: The sequence 1, 2, 4, … is geometric. What is the 6th term?
items.e: Keep multiplying by 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. The 6th term is 32.

items.e: Divide a term by the one before: 50 ÷ 10 = 5.

sets.title: Means, sum to infinity and problems

items.q: Find the arithmetic mean of 49 and 3.
Find the geometric mean of 81 and 324.
The A.M. and G.M. of two positive numbers are 74 and 24. Find the numbers.
items.e: a + b = 148 and ab = 576, so a and b are the roots of t² − 148t + 576 = 0: 4 and 144. (A.M. ≥ G.M.: 74 ≥ 24.)

items.q: Insert 3 numbers between 2 and 162 so that the resulting sequence is a G.P.
items.e: 162 = 2 × r4, so r = 3. The numbers are 6, 18, 54.

items.q: The A.M. and G.M. of two positive numbers are 61 and 11. Find the numbers.
items.e: a + b = 122 and ab = 121, so a and b are the roots of t² − 122t + 121 = 0: 1 and 121. (A.M. ≥ G.M.: 61 ≥ 11.)

items.q: Insert 3 numbers between 3 and 243 so that the resulting sequence is a G.P.
items.e: 243 = 3 × r4, so r = 3. The numbers are 9, 27, 81.

items.q: Find the sum of the infinite geometric series 12 + 6 + 3 + …, if it exists.
items.e: |r| = |12| < 1, so the sum is a1/(1 − r) = 12 ÷ (1 − 12) = 24.

items.q: Find the sum of the infinite geometric series 8 − 163 + 329 + …, if it exists.
items.e: |r| = |−23| < 1, so the sum is a1/(1 − r) = 8 ÷ (1 − (−23)) = 245.

items.q: Find the sum of the infinite geometric series 2 + 25 + 225 + …, if it exists.
items.e: |r| = |15| < 1, so the sum is a1/(1 − r) = 2 ÷ (1 − 15) = 52.

items.q: Find the sum of the infinite geometric series 10 + 6 + 185 + …, if it exists.
items.e: |r| = |35| < 1, so the sum is a1/(1 − r) = 10 ÷ (1 − 35) = 25.

items.q: Find the sum of the infinite geometric series 6 − 9 + 272 + …, if it exists.
items.e: r = −32 and |r| ≥ 1, so the terms do not shrink and the series diverges. The sum does not exist.

items.q: Find the sum of the infinite geometric series 5 + 52 + 54 + …, if it exists.
items.e: |r| = |12| < 1, so the sum is a1/(1 − r) = 5 ÷ (1 − 12) = 10.

items.q: Logs are stacked with 22 in the bottom row, 21 in the next row, 20 in the row after that, and so on, up to 5 logs in the top row. How many logs are there in the stack?
items.e: There are 18 rows: S = n/2 (first + last) = 18/2 (22 + 5) = 243.

items.q: A hall has 20 seats in the first row and 4 more seats in each next row. There are 15 rows. How many seats are there in all?
Logs are stacked with 20 in the bottom row, 19 in the next row, 18 in the row after that, and so on, up to 10 logs in the top row. How many logs are there in the stack?
items.e: There are 11 rows: S = n/2 (first + last) = 11/2 (20 + 10) = 165.
